title: Headcount crossover - pricing sensitivity and credit tilt (Q3 pilot)
summary: One-page budgeting snapshot modeling three scenarios where shifts between fractional hires and full-time equivalents (FTE), combined with a targeted credit-tilt pricing experiment, change monthly burn and SLA-adjusted unit economics. Purpose: give FP&A + Product a quick decision surface for a Q3 sprint pilot.
body:
Context and goal:
We need a compact decision surface for a Q3 pilot that trades small headcount flex (fractional engineers / SREs / infra contractors) against two pricing levers: a credit-tilt bundle for high-token customers and a micro-price reduction for mid-tier routes. The aim is to understand near-term monthly burn impact and unit margin per 1M tokens.

Document structure: overview -> assumptions -> scenario outputs (tables) -> sensitivity narrative -> recommended pilot design and action items. This is a working sheet; numbers are first-pass and meant to stimulate ops tradeoffs.

Key financial metrics included in the tables below: incremental monthly burn, delta FTE (net hires / swaps), expected revenue delta from price moves, and break-even months for experiment cost. All formulas are simple and spelled out next to the table rows.

Notes on interpretation: run rate numbers assume current committed capacity; we do NOT assume additional GPU purchases — fractional headcount impacts are mostly orchestration, monitoring and on-call overhead, not raw infra costs. Pricing changes are revenue-facing and modeled conservatively (50% adoption in affected segments during pilot).

Quick formula reference used in tables: 
- incremental_monthly_burn = (net_fte_cost + contractor_cost) - (reallocated_budget)
- revenue_delta = base_monthly_route_revenue * adoption_pct * (price_delta_pct)
- unit_margin_per_1M_tokens = (route_revenue_after_change - incremental_infra_costs_per_1M) / 1 (expressed per 1M tokens)

Caveat: token-mix shifts can materially change per-token infra costs; we used current token distribution from Product (Feb snapshot) but will re-run with new eval sets if pilot is approved.
key_tables: C-Combined,+5% on credit tilt and -4% mid-tier,50, -1, 12000, 0, +8, NA
assumptions: Average fully-burdened FTE monthly cost = $18,000 (salaries + benefits + G&A allocation)
Typical fractional contractor slot = $7,500/month (specialized infra/ops contractor)
High-token cohort baseline monthly route revenue = $560,000; mid-tier route baseline monthly revenue = $300,000
Adoption_pct for pilot pricing moves assumed 50% of eligible customers during 12-week pilot window
Infrastructure marginal cost per 1M tokens (current mix) = $3,500; assumed unchanged for headcount swaps in this pilot
No additional GPU commit or decommit assumed for the pilot period (capacity neutral)
Credit-tilt is treated as additive revenue (customers buy credit bundles) rather than a discount unless explicitly modeled as price_change
All dollar figures are USD and rounded to nearest $1k for this quick sheet
model_parameters: elasticity_high_token = -0.6 (assumed sensitivity of demand to effective per-token price in high-token cohort)
scenario_overview: Baseline: No pricing or headcount changes — used as sanity-check and to anchor incremental comparisons.

A - CreditTilt: Offer 10% more bundled credits to our top 20 customers by token usage. Expect net headcount reduction of 2 FTE (shift to automation + batching suggested by Optimize team), contractor spend to cover rollout oversights. Net monthly burn improves; revenue_delta modeled as +5% effective revenue on high-token routes after bundle uptake.

B - MidTierCut: Small per-token reduction for mid-tier routes (-7%). This is aimed at stimulating demand in the mid-market. Modeled as +1 FTE in support/CS and increased contractor monitoring. Short-term burn increases; longer-term ARR upside is uncertain and depends on adoption and retention uplift.

C - Combined: Conservative blended move (+5% credit tilt revenue, -4% mid-tier price) with one net FTE reduction (offset by contractors). This is the low-risk middle path; modeled to be roughly budget neutral with minor revenue upside from credit-bundle uptake.
sensitivity_notes: If elasticity_mid_tier is more elastic (-1.2), scenario B loses revenue and breakeven extends beyond 6 months — downside risk substantial.
Credit-tilt adoption under 30% reduces revenue_delta materially; bundle design must ensure perceived value to reach 50% adoption assumption.
Headcount swaps are operationally feasible only if Product/Optimize commits two sprint cycles to automation improvements; otherwise contractor costs climb by ~20% to compensate.

A 10% increase in infra_cost_per_1M tokens (e.g., from token mix or regional GPU price rise) pushes all scenarios' unit margin down by ~+$350 per 1M tokens — equivalent to ~10–15% margin erosion on modeled routes.
recommended_pilot_design: Pilot length: 12 weeks (Q3 sprint slice) with midpoint check at week 6
Scope: top-20 high-token customers for credit-tilt; 40 mid-tier customers for mid-tier cut A/B test
Instrumentation: per-route token telemetry + delta-revenue tagging + cohort retention flagging; tie to Redwood Console dashboards
Headcount plan: commit to 1 contractor slot for rollout week 0-6, reduce two FTEs as automation flows are validated week 6-12 (soft hiring freeze safe-guards apply)
Decision gate: if revenue_delta_monthly < 60% of modeled after 6 weeks, rollback price move and reallocate contractor to conversion work
action_items: Finance: finalize detailed month-by-month cash flow for pilot (due 2026-03-10) using product telemetry export
Product/Optimize: produce automation backlog with clear acceptance criteria tied to the 2 FTE reduction claim (due 2026-03-05)
GTM/CS: prepare customer-facing language for credit bundles and mid-tier trial communications (draft by 2026-03-08)
SRE: validate no infra capacity expansion required for pilot and confirm marginal infra_cost_per_1M assumption (due 2026-03-04)
Legal: quick T&C check for credit bundle changes (low-risk) - confirm by 2026-03-09
open_questions: What is the realistic minimum adoption we can guarantee for the credit bundle (sales commitments)?
If mid-tier price reduction triggers demand doubling, do we have capacity headroom in region us-west-2?
Are there accounting implications for treating credits as additive revenue vs deferred revenue for the bundle? Finance to advise.
Is there appetite from the People team to reallocate two open infra hiring slots to automation work vs backfilling?
